target_customer: Wholesale distributors, starting with industrial, building materials and textile distributors
problem: Distributors run inventory planning, purchasing and customer service by hand across ERPs and inboxes.
business_model: B2B SaaS for distributors, sits on top of the existing ERP
product_category: AI agents for supply chain operations

founders.name: Alex Tung
founders.background_notes: YC page says he helped Ankar reach seven figure ARR in under a year.

founders.name: Leon Yao
founders.background_notes: YC page says he published AI robotics research at IROS as an undergraduate.

competitors.name: Netstock
competitors.what: Inventory planning software with an AI Pack for SMBs and wholesale

competitors.name: StockIQ
competitors.what: Planning software that launched an AI agent called Edison

technical_complexity.rationale: Demand forecasting plus ERP integration and agent workflows are standard with hard parts in messy data.

defensibility.rationale: ERP integration and learned buyer behavior create some lock in, but incumbents and startups were adding AI agents at the same time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Planning vendors were already shipping AI features in 2026. No takeover of Whitespace found.

market_need_then: Distribution industry research cited by Modern Distribution Management shows 400 plus distributors investing in AI, indicating demand.

identity.logo: Logo mark with wordmark, per company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain spoken with short confident headlines

branding.community_and_virality: Customer testimonials only on own site

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word with many same name companies; no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Whitespace is an early Summer 2026 company selling AI inventory planning to wholesale distributors. Two named customers appear on its site and a third party reports ARR growth during the batch, but there is no verified funding or exit. Differentiation against established planning vendors adding AI will decide the outcome, and the founders have supply chain and AI backgrounds.
notes: Unverified: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round, seen only on that aggregator, so no round recorded. Outcome search returned only same name companies (for example a Verisk Sequel acquisition of an insurance Whitespace), which are unrelated. Location conflict: YC says San Francisco, some sources say London. Competitor source dates are year only. Completeness pass: the $125K seed is recorded from Dealroom alone (page labeled made with AI, no date, no investors); it likely matches the YC standard deal. A $3.2M seed (CB Insights, MaC Venture Capital) and a $13.2M Series A (2025-11) found in search appear to belong to different companies named Whitespace and are not recorded.
